body:
PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by #1744, and NOT a privilege-boundary crossing. Raised by the
security review of #1744 for awareness, and recorded here so it is not rediscovered.

`root/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/cwa-ingest-service/run:40` does
`echo $((timeout_minutes * 60))` where `timeout_minutes` comes from
`sqlite3 /config/cwa.db "SELECT ingest_timeout_minutes FROM cwa_settings LIMIT 1;"`.
Bash arithmetic contexts recursively evaluate variable contents, so a non-numeric value
there is a shell-eval primitive rather than a parse error. Sibling reads in the same file
share the shape.

Why it is NOT being fixed as part of #1744:
- the value is settable only by an operator/admin who already commands the conversion
  pipeline, so no privilege boundary is crossed;
- #1744 neither introduced it nor made it more reachable, and widening that PR's scope
  would have obscured the shutdown fix it exists to deliver.

Fix direction when someone does take it: validate the DB value as an integer before it
reaches `$(( ))` — e.g. `case $v in (*[!0-9]*|'') v=15;; esac` — rather than relying on
the column's intended type. Cheap, and it removes the class rather than this instance.

resolution.note: Shipped in #2121: every DB-sourced number in cwa-ingest-service passes an arithmetic-free validator before use; s6 audit found no other DB-to-arithmetic path.

title: cwa-ingest-service evaluates a DB-sourced value in an arithmetic context (shell-eval primitive)
